INSERT INTO adds a row: name the columns, then give the values in the same order. Text goes between single quotes: INSERT INTO products (name, price, stock) VALUES ('{item}', {price}, {stock});
INSERT INTO stock (item, qty) VALUES ('{item}', {n}) ON CONFLICT(item) DO UPDATE SET qty = qty + excluded.qty;  Try it on a copy: cp stock.db test.db; sqlite3 test.db < {file}

INSERT … ON CONFLICT(item) DO UPDATE tries the insert, and when the item already exists (item is the PRIMARY KEY) runs the update instead: an "upsert". In the update, excluded.qty is the qty you tried to insert. INSERT OR REPLACE is not the same: it deletes the old row, so the old qty and the shelf are lost.
